info.title: dotnet-runic
info.description: Generated-command development coordination for Runic Views Window projects.

commands.name: pack
commands.description: Package a directory as a Runic asset archive.

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Asset paths to omit, separated by semicolons. Repeatable.

options.name: --trusted-generated-output
options.description: Snapshot trusted build output; works on any OS.

options.name: --no-default-excludes
options.description:
Also pack .git directories and .env* files, which are left out by
default.

options.name: --entry-point
options.description: Entry document relative to the source directory. [default: index.html]

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version

options.name: --format
options.description: Select output format

arguments.name: SOURCE_DIRECTORY
arguments.description:
Directory to package, usually a frontend build output such as dist.
[required]

arguments.name: DESTINATION_ARCHIVE
arguments.description: Archive file to write; it is replaced atomically. [required]

commands.name: completion
commands.description: Generate bash, zsh, fish or PowerShell completions

commands.name: dev
commands.description: Run the application with development watchers.

options.name: --no-restore
options.description:
Skip the .NET restore and the JavaScript package install. The build does
not install missing frontend packages either.

options.name: --no-frontend-watch
options.description:
Build the frontend once instead of starting its development server or
watcher.

options.name: --no-dotnet-watch
options.description:
Run the application once instead of restarting it under dotnet watch
after C# edits.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description:
Print the evaluated project configuration and exit without changing files
or starting processes.

options.name: --no-build
options.description:
Skip the .NET restore and build before the Window starts, as dotnet run
--no-build does. dotnet watch still builds after C# edits.

options.name: --environment
options.description:
Set an environment variable for the Window process, as dotnet run -e
does. Repeat it for several variables.

options.name: --project
options.description:
The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
current directory.

options.name: --configuration
options.description: The build configuration. [default: Debug]

options.name: --launch-profile
options.description:
Run the Window with this profile from Properties/launchSettings.json. By
default dev uses no launch profile.

options.name: --verbosity
options.description:
The MSBuild verbosity of the builds the command runs: q[uiet], m[inimal],
n[ormal], d[etailed] or diag[nostic]. Without it, each command uses its
own default. [choices: q, quiet, m, minimal, n, normal, d, detailed,
diag, diagnostic]

options.name: --aot
options.description:
With --runtime, check a publish with -p:PublishAot=true.
[conflicts: no-aot]

options.name: --no-aot
options.description:

[conflicts: aot]

options.name: --self-contained
options.description:
With --runtime, check a publish with --self-contained true.
[conflicts: no-self-contained]

options.name: --no-self-contained
options.description:
With --runtime, check a publish with --self-contained false.
[conflicts: self-contained]

options.name: --project
options.description:
The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
current directory.

options.name: --configuration
options.description:
The build configuration to evaluate. Defaults to Debug, or Release
with --runtime as dotnet publish does.

options.name: --fail-on
options.description:
Fail when a check reaches this status: never, fail or warn. Defaults
to fail in both output modes.

options.name: --runtime
options.description:
Also check deployment prerequisites for this runtime identifier, for
example linux-x64, win-x64 or osx-arm64.

commands.name: flathub
commands.description:
Write a Flathub source-build manifest with offline NuGet and npm sources from the
committed lock files. --build builds it with flatpak-builder on Linux.

options.name: --build
options.description:
Build the manifest as Flathub does: install the runtime and SDK
extensions, download the sources, then build offline and write a bundle.
Linux only.

options.name: --git-url
options.description: The application's git repository, which Flathub checks out. [required]

commands.name: macos
commands.description:
Package the application as an .app bundle in a disk image, and with --pkg an installer
package. Runs on macOS.

options.name: --sandbox
options.description:
Sign the bundle for the App Sandbox, which the Mac App Store
requires, as RunicMacSandbox does: the sandbox, loopback network,
user-selected files and bookmark entitlements.

options.name: --pkg
options.description:
Also write an installer package with productbuild that installs
the bundle in /Applications, as App Store Connect takes it.

options.name: --project
options.description:
The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
current directory.

options.name: --configuration
options.description: The build configuration to publish. [default: Release]

options.name: --runtime
options.description:
The runtime identifier to publish for. Defaults to the host's
architecture on the target's operating system. Runic supports
osx-arm64 (Apple silicon) only.

options.name: --output-directory
options.description:
The directory to write the package to. Defaults to
artifacts/package/<target> beside the project.

options.name: --sign
options.description:
Sign with this identity from the keychain instead of ad hoc:
Developer ID Application, or Apple Distribution for the Mac App
Store.

options.name: --notary-profile
options.description:
Notarize and staple the disk image, and a signed installer
package, with this notarytool keychain profile. [requires: sign]

options.name: --provisioning-profile
options.description:
Embed this provisioning profile as
Contents/embedded.provisionprofile and sign with its application
and team identifiers. [requires: sign]

options.name: --installer-sign
options.description:
Sign the installer package with this installer identity from the
keychain, such as 3rd Party Mac Developer Installer or Developer
ID Installer. [requires: pkg]

commands.description: Measure a published application and write a size report.

options.name: --aot
options.description: Publish with Native AOT, the default. [conflicts: no-aot]

options.name: --no-aot
options.description: Publish without Native AOT. [conflicts: aot]

options.name: --verify-argument
options.description:
An argument for the --verify executable. Repeat it for several
arguments.

options.name: --self-contained
options.description:
Publish self-contained, the default.
[conflicts: no-self-contained]

options.name: --no-self-contained
options.description:
Publish framework-dependent, with -p:SelfContained=false, for
example to compare with a self-contained build. Combine it with

options.name: --property
options.description:
Pass an MSBuild property to the evaluation and publish, as dotnet
publish -p does, for example OptimizationPreference=Speed. Repeat
it for several properties. Configuration, RuntimeIdentifier,
PublishAot and SelfContained have their own options.

options.name: --project
options.description:
The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
current directory.

options.name: --runtime
options.description:
The runtime identifier to publish for, for example linux-x64.
Required.

options.name: --configuration
options.description: The build configuration. [default: Release]

options.name: --report
options.description:
The JSON report to write. The file must not exist yet. Default:
runic-size-<runtime>-<UTC time>.json in the current directory.

options.name: --verify
options.description:
An executable to run after a successful publish, as a path or a
command on PATH, such as node. It receives the --verify-argument
values, then the publish directory and the published application's
path. A nonzero exit code fails the command.

options.name: --verbosity
options.description:
The MSBuild verbosity of the builds the command runs: q[uiet],
m[inimal], n[ormal], d[etailed] or diag[nostic]. Without it, each
command uses its own default. [choices: q, quiet, m, minimal, n,
normal, d, detailed, diag, diagnostic]
